external_entities.name: developer
external_entities.description: A person who writes changes, pushes branches, and can manually trigger rebuilds.
external_entities.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
external_entities.notes: The text does not state the developer's trust zone or authentication details.

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: The public package registry reached during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: Picks up merges, fetches source, resolves dependencies, produces container images, pushes images, and calls the deploy controller.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: Maintains the current release selection for the estate and answers store server and build runner requests.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small back-office server that polls the deploy controller, pulls a changed image, and restarts the till software container.
processes.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
processes.notes: The description refers to about 1,200 store servers collectively.

processes.name: till software
processes.description: Software running as a container on each store server.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container

data_stores.name: git server
data_stores.description: The self-hosted Git server receiving developer branches and providing source for builds.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the git server encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: The registry storing finished container images tagged with commit SHAs.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: current release record
data_stores.description: The record identifying which image SHA the estate should be running.
data_stores.source_excerpt: holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: Developer branch data sent to the Git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner retrieves source from the Git server after a merge.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: The build runner uploads a finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.data_description: container image tagged with the commit SHA

data_flows.name: make current release
data_flows.description: The build runner asks the deploy controller to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release
data_flows.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.

data_flows.name: ask current release
data_flows.description: A store server asks the deploy controller which release is current.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: The text does not say what a store server presents to the controller.

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server retrieves the selected container image from the registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: it pulls that image from the registry and restarts the container
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it.

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner retrieves dependencies from the public package registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.

data_flows.name: kick off rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and manually starts a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network hosting the Git server and deploy controller.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: The separate environment hosting the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: The in-store estate containing the store servers and till software.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The image registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: retail WAN
trust_boundaries.description: The WAN carrying traffic between stores and the corporate network.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Traffic between the stores and the corporate network goes over the retail WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The external network reached by dependency resolution.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the public package registry on the internet

assumptions.assumption: The build runner, store server, till software, image registry, and release data carry business-critical release data because the text describes container images and the estate's current release.
assumptions.basis: The build runner produces and transfers the container image that is deployed across the estate; releases are business-critical data.

assumptions.assumption: The deploy controller holds business-critical release data.
assumptions.basis: The controller maintains which image SHA the estate should run; releases are business-critical data.

assumptions.assumption: The store server touches business-critical release data.
assumptions.basis: The store server queries the current release and pulls the selected image.

assumptions.assumption: The till software is associated with business-critical estate software.
assumptions.basis: The till software runs on the in-store estate and is deployed as the container image whose release is managed.

assumptions.assumption: The image registry holds business-critical release artifacts.
assumptions.basis: It stores finished container images used to deploy the estate; releases are business-critical data.

assumptions.assumption: The current release record holds business-critical release data.
assumptions.basis: The record identifies the image release the estate should run.

assumptions.assumption: The image publication flow carries business-critical release artifacts.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries the finished container image used as an estate release.

assumptions.assumption: The build-runner release request carries business-critical release data.
assumptions.basis: The request identifies the image to make current for the estate.

assumptions.assumption: The store-server release query carries business-critical release data.
assumptions.basis: The query concerns which release the estate should run.

assumptions.assumption: The image-pull flow carries business-critical release artifacts.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries the container image deployed to the store estate.

assumptions.assumption: The manual rebuild request concerns business-critical release data.
assumptions.basis: The request starts a rebuild of main for the in-store deployment pipeline.
